about: Design Infra's rulings on how Wonder Blocks is meant to be used (Judge Trudy). Each verdict is tied to a component in code, links to the guideline that covers it when one exists, and otherwise carries its own reason and is listed as missing guidance. Read by the ka-prototype-builder audit; only entries with status 'confirmed' and approved_by from a ruler are applied. Changes need review from the code owners of this folder.
self_ruling: A Design Infra member may rule on a request they raised; no second ruler is required.

entries.reason: ActivityIconButton's `label` prop with its documented `styles` prop (root / label), setting position and margins only, so the tooltip centres on the button. Layout through style props is what Wonder Blocks expects.
entries.source: Caitlyn Mayers, practice display settings prototype, 2026-10-27
entries.guidance_needed: Customizing components: layout through a component's documented styles prop (position, margins, size, alignment) isn't drift; visual overrides (colour, border, radius, shadow, type) are
entries.ruling_text: This is not an issue, evidence is correct.

entries.title: Practice content panel: no Wonder Blocks scaffolding component for this surface
entries.prod: ContentPanelCard, the practice page's main surface, is built on WB Card.
entries.suggested_wb: Not in Wonder Blocks yet. Wonder Blocks likely needs a set of scaffolding components that give componentized versions of surfaces like the practice container. Until they exist, this is known debt: don't swap Card for a hand-built View-and-tokens surface.
entries.guideline: Surfaces and elevations describes this surface (content panel / question card: Surface 2, Low elevation on a busy practice page) but not which component builds it.
entries.source: Caitlyn Mayers, practice display settings prototype, 2026-10-27
entries.follow_up: Candidate for a WB scaffolding component set: run wonder-blocks-candidacy-eval.
entries.ruling: Wonder Blocks gap: likely needs scaffolding components (e.g. the practice container surface). Not a component swap.
entries.gap: Scaffolding components for page surfaces like the practice content panel
entries.guidance_needed: Which component builds a page surface like the practice content panel (Surface 2)
entries.ruling_text: Finding is correct, the card is not appropriate but this is flagged as a need to add to WB as some form of scaffolding component.

entries.reason: The drawing toolbar's close button removes two corner radii so it attaches to the tool group it opens and closes. This attached-toggle pattern is used only here, so Wonder Blocks doesn't need to accommodate it; the control's design isn't the problem.
entries.source: Caitlyn Mayers, practice display settings prototype, 2026-10-28

quality_issues.summary: Drawing toolbar close button: accessible name changes with layout and mixes disclosure and action semantics
quality_issues.detail: The close button carries aria-expanded="true" as a disclosure toggle, but its accessible name changes by layout: "Draw" in the vertical toolbar (visible label next to an X icon; tooltip "Close drawing tools") and "Close drawing tools" in the horizontal toolbar, announced as "Close drawing tools, expanded". Pick one pattern: a disclosure named "Draw" with aria-expanded in every layout, or a "Close drawing tools" action with no aria-expanded, and make the visible label, icon and tooltip agree with it.
quality_issues.decision: Not decided. Logged only; Design Infra decides later what to do, and nothing is filed until then.

entries.reason: This drawing toolbar's colour picker is a native <input type="color">. Using the browser default is expected for this control: the browser handles it with system defaults. The ruling covers this one instance only; it isn't a general rule about native controls.
entries.source: Caitlyn Mayers, practice display settings prototype, 2026-10-28
entries.ruling_text: *Ruling:* Not an issue. Using the browser default is expected here: it's handled by the browser, uses system defaults, and allows us to benefit from a reusable component without the cost of building and maintaining one ourselves. I'll allow it.
